title: The Cord That Keeps a Count

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A bundle is counted in the arm that carries it. The hands that cut it are counted in nothing at all.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the reed-cutters, the Weir

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-twenty-to-one-hundred-and-twenty-two-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (a length of cord read as a record kept where no thumb will read it, the yard going around an empty place read as a chart closed with a neat line over a note never opened, the damper's double bite read as the clamp that holds and the clamp that takes, the held breath read as a breath stopped against iron) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, Waiting Room, collector or back-room interior

scenes.title: A Direction, Not a Figure
scenes.synopsis: First entry, Day 120, Reed 1, Firstday, at the going of the light in the yard at Low Kiln and at the edge of the worked strips east of it. The planting month is behind and the yard turns toward the reed beds and the Weir; the first reed-cutting work is spoken of as a direction and a going-downriver and never as a figure, as the planting once was, bundles to be counted in glances and armfuls when there are any. The yard goes around its two kept lines --- the clean dark line and the new finer grey called the thaw --- and around the space beneath the lowest rack, and the missing hand's place in the worked strip is still gone around with a look, a wide step and no number (T098 carried, not paid: no name, no cause, no body, no figure). A woman come up from the strips asks what the reeds will cost now that the hands are out of them; Sella glances once at the clay jar and sends her to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, as she sent a woman to the pot in Seed (T058/T079, T071/T072, T009/T013/T092). The boy, one hundred and twenty days old and four months, carried at the half-pace from every open slate, reads the going-around of the field's empty place as a chart closed with a neat line over a note never opened, exact, complete and worth nothing, and sets it on a place of its own, laying no likeness across the shelf's two gaps, the fold's one crust or the empty place at his ear. Advances T098 (carried), T071/T072, T009/T013/T092, T058/T079, T060/T086. Withheld: no name, no cause, no body, no figure, no third gap, no cause made from a likeness, no ending.

scenes.title: The Pot Has Said It
scenes.synopsis: Second entry continued, Day 120, evening under the Vail kiln-house roof and at the loaf shelf. Sella gives the bucket, broom, pot and fire their instructions before anybody and never the basket, says the house where another woman would say I, and goes wide around the space beneath the lowest rack as though it were a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it. She moves her lips along the loaf row without a figure and does not touch the widow's mark, because a shelf is not an opening; the shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps --- the old space at the row's end and the new palm's breadth that came in the night of Seed 6 --- in a room that does not touch the fold's one stiff brown-edged crust and its unnamed empty place. At the going of the light she sets the boy on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, because nobody under the roof has been given an instruction about the thread. She tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, and pushes a strand of coal-black hair back with the wrist that carries the little-door burn, the grey streak pale. The boy finds the file unchanged: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals, the told bell beside the heard bell, the word forty unspoken, and the hand that did not come back held on a place of its own. He adds the day's two objects --- the reed work named as a direction and the woman sent to the pot --- on places of their own and lays no finger across them. Advances T058/T079, T060/T086, T061/T082, T071/T072 (120). Withheld: no joining of the two shelf gaps to the fold's gap, no figure, no seventh, no ending.

scenes.title: The Bite and the Seventh Year
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, Day 121, Reed 2, Secondday, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed and its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the damper and the Clay Yard. Men unnamed come up the yard with their collars high and speak low in the back room; Jorra Vail gives the house no name for them and does not say the room was cold. He comes through with fine grey slate dust ground into both forearms past the bent little finger, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone (It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady) and tells a pot You'll do. When Sella has not finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of her sentence and the household straightens around his silence the way cloth straightens when a weight is lifted. The boy reads the iron once more as the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, and files it as an object worth nothing joined to no kiln (T035/T031/T062). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed; his seventh year is pressed past the end of the planting and still held, the small knife at the very edge with six counted and the seventh nearly gone, the unforged collector sentence beside it and the breath from Seed 16 still unspent with a small interval at the top of each reach (T036/T076). His stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check and neither man names the other's silence; the loan that can hear is uncalled. Advances T035/T031/T062, T036/T076, T071/T072 (121). Withheld: no calling of the loan, no spending of the seventh year, no name for the men, no fourth telling, no ending.

scenes.title: The Half-Beat After the Knock
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry continued, Day 121, midday and going of the light at the market stalls beyond the Cross and the out-of-line landing below the north bridge. The soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the landing with his cuff grey from washing and his slate to his forearm for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, and the market sells its reeds and eels over the top of him as though a man with a slate were a thing a landing always had (T090/T080). At the market's edge a foundling is glimpsed once, unnamed and silent, in cast-off clothes worn like a uniform, silt dried pale in the creases of his wrists and a green sliver of lead-glaze on a string at his throat that catches the light when he turns and goes dull when he turns back. When a kiln-hand sets a pot down, his head goes toward it a half-beat after the boy's, after the knuckle and after the note, then stops in the middle of the turn; he rubs the sliver twice with his thumb and his mouth opens on the tail of a sentence and nothing comes out that any clerk could take down. No loaf passes and no slate is seen. The boy files the delay as a thing that comes after the knock and is not a hearing, beside his own turning and the watcher's late turn, joined to neither, and does not call it a sale (T033/T034). Advances T090/T080, T033/T034, T071/T072 (121). Withheld: no loaf, no slate, no sale, no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, no name for the child, no ending.

scenes.title: The Cord at the Weir
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, Day 122, Reed 3, Thirdday, morning downriver at the Weir and going of the light under the Vail roof. The reed-cutters work their first bundles into the yard, counted in glances and armfuls and never in a figure. At the Weir the boy, carried at the edge of the work where no slate lies, glimpses a reed-cutter's tally kept in a length of cord in a material no Court thumb will read: **T099 planted here**, a third private record in the district, held for the far-off day it is laid beside Mira's grey cord and the second twist beneath it, Orra Weir's knot-string lying beside Mira's board and not touching it, Alda Reed's six hidden pages in the little tin, and Dessa Silt's pewter tin above the abandoned bed (T059/T025/T024, T023/T089). Orra may be glimpsed at the Weir beside her board and still watched, unnamed in the narration and not asked; the word forty stays unspoken. Rusk is spoken of only as the man who walks the Weir at dusk, not fully introduced. The cord is carried and not counted: no figure is read, no knot is counted, no joining is made to the missing hand in the strip, and no name is given. Mira works the eels with pale slime dried in grey strokes on her sleeves and does not look into the basket; her board lies beside Orra's knot-string and does not touch it. Advances T099 (planted), T059/T025/T024, T023/T089, T061/T082, T071/T072 (122). Withheld: no figure read, no knot counted, no name, no joining to T098, no opening of tin or box, no word forty, no ending.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Twenty-Two
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry continued, Day 122, going of the light and the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof. Sella sets the boy on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool at his mouth frozen and unwiped, and lets her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed before it goes away. The door stands a finger's width open: the river's note of water over water comes through the gap and the carried fire's four, four and a gap comes through the floor under blind ash, its payer unnamed for a hundred and twenty-two days, the two sounds in two separate places and the three counts not become one. The boards overhead keep four nails, four, and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb. Under the roof the boy finds the file unchanged: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, three intervals, the told bell beside the heard bell, the word forty unspoken, the cold foot below the sill still the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T093/T094/T096), one stiff crust in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third, and the loaf shelf's two gaps in a room that does not touch. Nobody says he is one hundred and twenty-two days old. His count goes on into Day 123 unspent and spoken by nobody, and the hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down. Advances T071/T072 (122), T093/T094/T096, T060/T086, T097 (carried, not paid), T098 (carried), T099 (planted, unpaid). Withheld: no joining, no payment, no name, no seventh hearing, no third gap, no word forty, no ending.
